about.intro1: A ZX Spectrum emulator & programming environment for the browser. Source available <srcLink>here</srcLink>.
about.intro2: A related website is available at <zxplayLink>zxplay.org</zxplayLink>. ZX Play is a mobile-friendly ZX Spectrum emulator, for games.
about.legal: Please read <privacyLink>privacy policy</privacyLink> and <termsLink>terms of use</termsLink>, for this website.

bot.intro: Mention <botLink>@bot@zxplay.org</botLink> from Mastodon, or anywhere on the Fediverse, with a ZX Spectrum program and the bot replies with a video of the program running.
bot.howToAddress: Start your post with the bot's handle, then write the program after it. The mention must be the first thing in the post.
bot.howToReply: The bot replies with a video capture of the program running.
bot.machinesText: Add one of these hashtags to pick the machine. Without one, programs run on the 48K:
bot.languagesText: Without a language tag the program is treated as Sinclair BASIC (zmakebas). Add one of these hashtags to use another language:
bot.hashtagNote: Only these exact tags are read. Any other # stays part of the program, so PRINT #2 and #include work as normal.
bot.projectsText: Instead of writing code in the post, paste a link to a public project and the bot renders it directly. The link takes precedence over any code in the post, and a machine hint on the URL (?m=48 or ?m=128) wins over hashtags.
bot.limitVisibility: The reply uses the same visibility as your post.
bot.limitRate: Each account can make up to 10 requests per hour.
bot.limitCapture: The video captures up to 15 seconds of the program running.
bot.limitErrors: If the program does not compile, the bot replies with the compiler's error message.

debug.consolePlaceholder: type a command (try 'help', or view the Help tab)
debug.helpIntro: The console drives the engine's full debugger. Addresses and values take $ or 0x hex. The commands below are the ones that matter day to day; type help for the complete list.
debug.helpOutro: State-reading commands pause a running machine and leave it paused. Tracepoint hits and log-only port watches print to the browser's DevTools console.
debug.noBreakpoints: No breakpoints. Click a disassembly address marker or the editor gutter to add one.
debug.lineBpsPending: Source-line breakpoints need a source map — Play a sjasmplus project to arm them; address breakpoints from the disassembly pane always work.
debug.lineBpsStale: The source changed since the last compile, so line breakpoints are disarmed. Play to rebuild and re-arm them.
debug.panelNoData: No data yet — the panel refreshes when the machine pauses (breakpoint, step, or Pause).
